title: If the excited state survives: exothermic down-scattering signals in LZ's data and the lifetime window they exclude
question: If a relic fraction f2 of the excited state chi2 survives (P026: 0.42-0.50 at freeze-out), where do its exothermic down-scattering recoils land in LZ, what do LZ's ROI counts and the empty 600-1700 phd region imply for f2, tau(chi2), the dark-photon eps and m_A', could the 248 keV event itself be a down-scatter, and how does the exothermic rate modulate?
headline_result: A surviving chi2 down-scatters into a broad 70-330 keV spectrum (peak 155-180 keV, 59% in LZ's empty 125-200 keV bin, only 7-19% above the 270 keV edge); LZ's counts require f2(today) < 2.8e-3 (delta=300 keV) to 1.7e-7 (380 keV), tau(chi2) < 8.6-2.9e16 s and m_A' >= 2.39/0.92/0.53/0.25 GeV; 248 keV sits at the 97-99.7th percentile of the exothermic spectrum, so the event is a poor down-scatter candidate.
key_numbers: E*=267/312/326/339 keV, half-width 200-225 keV at 250 km/s; R_ROI=916/2.8e4/2.9e5/8.1e6 exothermic per endothermic event (iso; p 859 vs P011 858); f2<2.8e-3/5.7e-5/4.8e-6/1.7e-7; tau_min=8.4/4.8/3.8/2.9e16 s; m_A'>=2.39/0.92/0.53/0.25 GeV; eps>=4.2-4.7e-6 (alpha_D=0.1); 2.2-9 companions in 125-200 keV per 200-270 keV event; exothermic a1=2-5% vs endothermic 0.43-1.68
model_or_mechanism: pseudo-Dirac inelastic DM (isoscalar O1, dark-photon proton-only, Higgsino Z), exothermic chi2 N -> chi1 N with WimPyDD delta<0; joint Poisson likelihood over LZ regions
builds_on: LZ paper (Fig. 4, Fig. S4, MSSI table); P026, P011, P021, P038, P016, P002, P003, P006, P007, P014, P034; feeds P072
